tasks.short: Monitor file use and regulate access

steps.what: Flag computer files over the allowed total
Apply the signed access rule for files
Hold computer files that have no rule

tasks.design: File-class id and access totals sit on a {DATA_PLATFORM} view. A rule flags a class when the total exceeds the stored limit. The security analyst signs a tighter access rule. The {DATA_PLATFORM} applies that rule. The view is class totals, not a list of named people.
tasks.previous_blocker: File-use notes were screenshots and spreadsheets with no stable file-class id, so a limit could not be checked.
tasks.enabler_now: Access totals can be exported by file class with a stored limit, without naming a person.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a busy class should be tightened is a judgement, and a named-person view would be a different decision.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst regulates access for a file class and can leave a class unchanged.

ambition.what: Regulate a file class in the week its total crosses the limit, not at the quarterly review

tasks.altitude: Less time adding up use. The analyst keeps the right to refuse a tighter rule, and no named-person list is produced.

reach.task: Accept or challenge the file-class limit the analyst proposed
reach.learn: Which file classes were tightened and which totals are still over the limit

evidence.claim: Watching file use in a mid-size firm is a totals report plus a decision to tighten a class. Naming staff is a separate, heavier step.
Digest [S7] and [S8] describe a managed detection service for mid-size firms that uses models to speed investigation, while the analysts still decide.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. Class totals are enough for this decision. Contents of files are not.
Digest [S23] says a works council is consulted before staff monitoring. Access totals are not a view of named people, and this design does not add one.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so a file-class rule is not applied unattended.

assumptions: Focal role is the security analyst. The task regulates access for a file class after a signed rule. It does not score staff and it does not open a named-person view.
Input contract: file class id, access total, allowed total, system id, owner. Producer is the access-total export. A class with no allowed total is not flagged and is not tightened.
Use the data platform's own total and rule settings before custom code. A later request to name people waits for a works council. That request is out of this design.
unknowns: Whether the works council has already limited how file logs may be used.
Who owns a file class that spans two teams.
Whether this firm is in scope of the cyber duty of care.
research_questions: What share of file classes has no allowed total?
How often does a tightened class get relaxed the same month?

already_counted.description: Analyst still reads totals that the flag did not cover
Analyst decision time on whether to tighten a class

incremental.description: Set allowed totals when a new file class is added

approvals.approved_version: file class rule signed for this class id
the same signed file class rule

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most classes have no allowed total, so the flag does not fire and the analyst still reads totals by hand. The high case assumes totals are clean, while every tighten-or-leave decision stays with the analyst. Named-person review is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate system implementation with staff and vendors

steps.what: Draft implementation gaps from vendor notes

loop.input: vendor mail and plan item ids
loop.output: open items each citing one plan item id
loop.check: Every item id on the list is on the system plan
loop.stop: If the mail has no plan item id, leave it off the list and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Vendor sentences do not match item ids by a fixed table

steps.what: File the dates establishment personnel agreed

tasks.design: Outside vendors send item id, date and blocker by {EMAIL}. A bounded list in {DOCS} cites item ids from the system plan held on the {WORKFLOW} form. The security analyst meets establishment personnel and the vendors. Agreed dates are written back to that list. No live system change is applied from this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vendor mail and internal notes did not share a plan item id, so open points could not be lined up.
tasks.enabler_now: The system plan can list item ids that a vendor status mail can cite.
tasks.still_hard: What to slip, and what the establishment can accept from a vendor, is a meeting.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst coordinates the implementation dates with personnel and with outside vendors, and can reject a date.

ambition.what: Small vendors can post a dated status without waiting for a site visit

tasks.altitude: Less time merging mail into a list. The two conversations stay with the analyst, and nothing is changed on a live system here.

reach.task: Staff the implementation dates the analyst agreed
reach.learn: Which plan item ids have a date and which are still blocked

evidence.claim: Coordinating an implementation is mail plus meetings. A shared item id shortens the list. It does not hold the meeting.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and the duty of care for firms in scope includes supply-chain measures. Scope depends on sector and size.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so this task records dates and does not apply a vendor change on its own.

assumptions: Focal role is the security analyst. Establishment personnel are other_role. Outside vendors are supplier. The task ends at agreed dates. Installing the system is a later task.
Input contract: plan item id, vendor id, status date, blocker, system id. Producer is the vendor for status, and the plan owner for item ids. Mail with no plan item id is not added to the list.
Use the workflow form's own list and dates before custom code. The prior understates two separate conversations: one with personnel and one with vendors.
unknowns: Which vendors will use the status form.
Who may agree a date when the analyst is absent.
Whether this firm is in scope of supply-chain duties.
research_questions: What share of vendor mail cites no plan item id?
How often is an agreed date missed?

already_counted.description: Analyst fixes gap rows the extract got wrong
Personnel and vendor meetings stay with the analyst

incremental.description: Add plan item ids when the system plan gains a phase
Vendors resend status that cited no item id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes vendor mail stays free text, so the list rarely fills and the analyst still chases dates by hand. The high case assumes item ids are clean, while both meetings stay manual. No installation work is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train users and promote security awareness

steps.what: Choose topics for server and network efficiency

loop.output: awareness note that cites those policy ids
loop.check: Every topic on the note cites a policy id from the topic list
loop.stop: Drop a topic with no policy id and stop after one pass
loop.why_not_simpler: Local examples are not a fixed paragraph and stay with the analyst

steps.what: Sign the awareness note before the session
Record which users attended the session

tasks.design: Topic id and policy id come from {DOCS}. A bounded note drafts the awareness text from those ids only. The security analyst signs the note, then trains users in person and promotes the same points for server and network efficiency. Attendance is a name list on a {WORKFLOW} form, not a score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Awareness notes were rewritten from old slide files, so a session could not show which policy a point relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: Each topic can cite a policy id that the signed procedures document already uses.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a room of users understood the point, and which local example to use, is still the session.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst signs the note and delivers the session. Attendance is recorded. Nobody is scored.

ambition.what: New joiners get the same awareness session in their first month, not only at the yearly talk

tasks.altitude: Less time rebuilding the note. The analyst still stands in the room, and can refuse a topic that cites no policy.

reach.task: Apply the server and network points from the session
reach.learn: Which policy ids the signed awareness note cites

evidence.claim: Security awareness in a mid-size firm is a short note plus a live session. Completion can be a name list. Judging who understood is not a form field.
Digest [S16] says Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and includes a duty of care. Whether an awareness record is required depends on sector and size.
Digest [S3] says a document prompt can fill metadata and the fill can be wrong, so the note cites policy ids and the analyst still writes the examples.

assumptions: Focal role is the security analyst. The task ends after the live session and the attendance list. It does not score users and it does not change a server or a network setting.
Input contract: topic id, policy id, session date, audience, system id. Producer is the analyst from the signed policy document. A topic with no policy id is dropped from the note.
Use the document store's own pages and the workflow form's own attendance list before custom code. A learning record, if one exists, is configured before a second list.
unknowns: Whether a learning record already stores sessions.
Who delivers the session when the analyst is absent.
Whether this firm must keep attendance for a duty of care.
research_questions: What share of awareness topics cites no policy id?
How often is the yearly session the only one new joiners get?

already_counted.description: Analyst rewrites examples in the awareness note
The live session stays with the analyst

incremental.description: Add topic ids when a signed policy version changes

approvals.approved_version: awareness note signed for this session

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes topics have no policy id, so the note stays empty and the analyst still builds the session by hand. The high case assumes the note cites ids, while the sign-off and the live session stay manual. No assessment of users is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The analyst stops tallying file use by hand and chasing vendor mail, and keeps the time for access decisions, implementation meetings and live awareness sessions.
reach: Establishment personnel and outside vendors leave with dated implementation items, not an unattended system change.
System users attend a live awareness session based on a signed note, not a score of who failed.
skills_to_grow: Read file-class totals, not a ranking of named people.
Turn a vendor note into a plan item id and a date.
Sign the awareness note before the live session.
role.ambitious_version: File-class totals show where access should tighten, vendor dates are agreed in person, and awareness sessions stay live.
